conviction_note: The evidence is balanced. On the plus side, sell-side checks and script data point to a pharma-led revenue beat (RBC +1%, Guggenheim +0.5%) and the FY sales guide implies only about 3% H2 growth excluding the 53rd week, so it looks conservative. On the minus side are MedTech cardio (Abiomed Class I recalls and field actions, the UK study, EP competition and China VBP), a disputed EPS bar where a $1bn Firefly IPR&D charge will print as a 'miss' against stale consensus, and 2027 LOE/Sail dilution risk on the call. A name whose median print moves 0.9% and that sold a beat-and-raise in July (-2.7%) does not pay for beats. Findings sum to 0.0, p_up 50, abs_move 2.8 (options imply 3.0; the history median is 0.9). The two measurements agree on no direction.
bar: Revenue: consensus $25.29B (Hudson Labs, 2026-09-28, https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/johnson-johnson-q3-2026-earnings-preview-jnj-results), $25.37B (Zacks, cited by Guggenheim note https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/guggenheim-reiterates-johnson--johnson-stock-rating-ahead-of-earnings-93CH-4936583) and $25.38B (TipRanks, 2026-10-12, https://www.tipranks.com/news/johnson-johnson-stock-could-move-by-9-51-after-q3-results), so roughly $25.3-25.4B and agreeing. Adjusted EPS bar is DISPUTED: $2.48 (TIKR via Yahoo, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/johnson-johnson-stock-fell-nearly-152331021.html), $2.51 (AAII, 11 analysts), $2.52 (TipRanks), $2.66 (Zacks), $2.69 (Guggenheim's consensus), $2.81 (RBC's consensus). Informed estimates that include the Q3 Firefly/Sail IPR&D are $2.49 (Guggenheim), $2.53 (BofA) and $2.55 (RBC). Company guide: FY26 adj EPS $10.96-11.11 after the 2026-07-29 cut of $0.64 for Firefly ($0.46) and Sail ($0.18) (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000200406/000020040626000163/jnj-20260729.htm); FY reported sales $100.8-101.4B. Every EPS-dependent finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest is not crowded: 22.3M shares and 2.74 days to cover at the 2026-04-30 settlement (https://www.optionsanalysissuite.com/stocks/jnj/short-interest, no fresher settlement found), about 0.9% of float. Baseline skew is +1.85 vol points (mild put premium, priced_direction_lean 'balanced'), put/call OI 0.87. The event-implied move is 3.0% (straddle 3.3%; TipRanks 3.64%) against a historical median reaction of 0.9% over 7 prints, so options price more movement than the name has delivered. Tape: down about 5.9% from 9/28 to 10/2 (BofA warned Q3 EPS below Street, per Yahoo/TIKR 10/5), then +4.07% over 5 days to spot $263.23, -1.16% over 20 days, 5.5% below the 52-week high. No crowding in either direction.

findings.finding: Pharma-led revenue beat looks likely. RBC (2026-10-06) models Q3 sales 1% above consensus, with pharma 1.3% above on Tremfya and Icotyde. Guggenheim (2026-10-07) models $25.49B vs $25.37B consensus and cites strong script trends for Tremfya, Caplyta and Erleada, offset by Opsumit generic erosion. CFO Wolk (DB conference 9/17) said Icotyde had 17,000 patients after about 5 months with all three major PBMs covering it, and Tremfya IBD grew 80% in Q2. J&J beat Street sales in each of the last 5 quarters by 1.0-3.9%. The bar is about $25.3-25.4B; a print near $25.5-25.6B is about +0.5-1%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (7/15): sales $25.31B vs about $25.0B, adj EPS $2.90 vs $2.85, guide raised, and the stock fell 2.7% on MedTech softness and an HCA volume warning the same day. Q1 2026 beat-and-raise: +0.9%. Q3 2025 beat-and-raise plus ortho separation: -0.03%. The name has not paid for revenue beats.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The sell-side is publishing above-consensus sales, and J&J's 5-quarter beat streak is known, so a beat of about 1% is the expectation. A beat would be unpriced only if Icotyde or Tremfya land well above the 'north of 17,000 patients' framing. If it were fully priced, the consensus revenue line would already sit at $25.5B+; it sits at $25.3-25.4B.
findings.independence: Guggenheim script-data note (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/guggenheim-reiterates-johnson--johnson-stock-rating-ahead-of-earnings-93CH-4936583) and the Wolk DB transcript (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/johnson--johnson-at-deutsche-bank-healthcare-summit-growth-outlook-lifts-93CH-4906149) are separate sources. The beat-history fact comes from https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/johnson-johnson-stock-fell-nearly-152331021.html.

findings.finding: The FY26 reported-sales guide ($100.8-101.4B, midpoint $101.1B, unchanged on 7/29) minus H1 actuals ($24.1B Q1 + $25.31B Q2 = $49.4B) implies H2 of about $51.7B. That is about +6.4% vs H2 2025's about $48.6B, but 1.5-2 points of FY growth (about $1.4-1.9B) is the 53rd week (Wolk, 9/17), so the guide implies only about 3% H2 growth ex-extra-week, against H1 at +8.2% reported (about 6% operational). Q3 consensus of $25.3-25.4B (+5.5-5.8%) already runs above the guided pace, so a sales-guide raise is likely; J&J raised in Q3 2025, Q1 2026 and Q2 2026. RBC does not expect an EPS raise and says one would be bullish ahead of the 12/8 Enterprise Business Review.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Raises in April 2026 (+0.9%) and July 2026 (-2.7%) and Q3 2025 (-0.03%). Guidance raises have been expected and not paid for.
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is public, but every preview frames the bar as 'firm guidance', not a raise (asktraders 10/11; RBC expects no EPS raise). An adjusted-EPS raise above $11.11 despite the IPR&D would be the unpriced part. If priced, previews would carry a raised-range expectation; they do not.
findings.independence: H1 actuals come from the Q1 release (https://www.investor.jnj.com/investor-news/news-details/2026/Johnson--Johnson-reports-Q1-2026-results-raises-2026-outlook/) and the Q2 exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000200406/000020040626000146/a2026q2exhibit991.htm); the 53rd-week size comes from the Wolk DB transcript. RBC's view on a raise: https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/rbc-capital-raises-johnson--johnson-stock-price-target-on-pharma-strength-93CH-4933954. FX is a slight headwind: EUR/USD drifted to about 1.15 by mid-September vs about 1.168 in Q3 2025, and the guide assumed 1.15.

findings.finding: The adjusted-EPS headline will likely print below several published consensus figures ($2.66 Zacks, $2.69, $2.81) because the $1bn Firefly IPR&D charge (about $0.46/share) and the Sail charge (about $0.18) land in Q3 and are inside adjusted EPS. Informed estimates are $2.49-2.55; aggregators at $2.48-2.52 have caught up, others have not. Expect 'misses EPS' headlines pre-market, on a charge the company guided to on 7/29.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline print turned on an IPR&D-driven EPS miss. J&J guided the charge, and the RBC and BofA previews flagged that consensus does not fully reflect it.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The charge is in company guidance and in three broker previews, so only stale-consensus headline noise and algorithmic pre-market selling remain. That noise should fade by the close, which is why this is small.
findings.independence: BofA $2.53 / Guggenheim $2.49 / RBC $2.55 vs consensus (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/guggenheim-reiterates-johnson--johnson-stock-rating-ahead-of-earnings-93CH-4936583). This shares the 7/29 8-K with the guidance finding but lands on a different line: the reported-quarter headline, not the FY guide.

findings.finding: MedTech cardiovascular is the line that sank July and is set up weak again. US Impella demand fell 2% in Q2 after +14% in Q1, following a UK study questioning Impella in high-risk PCI. Abiomed then had Class I recalls posted June-July 2026 (Impella CP SmartAssist set, CP introducer kits, RP Flex). On 9/17 Wolk said J&J is working with the FDA on the field actions and guided a return to double-digit Abiomed growth only 'this time next year', implying a weak Q3 with a full quarter of impact. EP faces Farapulse competition, China VBP from H2 2026 (Hudson Labs), and RBC flagged EP 'competitive pressures and geopolitical headwinds' with MedTech only in line. Net of the rest: cardio is roughly 9-10% of sales and pharma (about 65%) is tracking above consensus, so this is sized as a narrative and segment-miss risk, not a revenue-bar risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: MedTech +3.6% operational, cardio/Abiomed softness, stock -2.7% on a beat-and-raise (Reuters via The Star, https://www.thestar.com.my/business/business-news/2026/07/17/jj-miss-overshadows-earnings-beat). This is the one line on which this name has recently been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the CFO flagged it and RBC models MedTech in line. Not fully priced because no preview quantifies Abiomed's Q3 decline or the combined effect of the recalls and the UK study over a full quarter. If priced, MedTech consensus would have been cut and previews would call cardio a known miss; they say 'MedTech expected to improve in H2' (asktraders 10/11).
findings.independence: FDA recall notice (https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/medical-device-recalls-and-early-alerts/heart-pump-recall-abiomed-removes-impella-cp-sets-smartassist), the Q2 Impella data (The Star/Reuters 2026-07-17), RBC's EP comment (investing.com 10/06) and the China VBP risk (Hudson Labs 9/28) are separate sources.

findings.finding: Bloomberg reported on 2026-09-11 that Apollo was in advanced talks to buy DePuy Synthes (orthopaedics, about $9.3B 2025 sales, about 1% growth) for about $20B, with 'an agreement could be reached within several weeks'. No deal was announced as of early October and EDGAR shows no 8-K since 8/4. J&J announced the ortho separation alongside Q3 2025 results on 2025-10-14, so the Q3 release is a demonstrated venue for this news. A cash sale at about 2.1x sales of a low-growth unit would bring clarity, roughly $20B to redeploy, and a margin lift.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-10-14: the ortho separation was announced with Q3 results and the stock moved -0.03%. Portfolio news has not moved this name much on the day.
findings.why_not_priced: The talk is known; whether it lands this morning is not. If the market expected an announcement on the print, implied vol would be well above 3% and previews would lead with it; previews mention it only in passing ('no agreement as of early October', Yahoo 10/5).

findings.finding: The call is likely to carry first 2027 colour, as J&J did on its Q3 2025 call, ahead of the 12/8 Enterprise Business Review, and 2027 has three known headwinds. First, $4-4.5B of LOE (Xarelto about $2B, PAH about $1.5B, Simponi and Stelara about $1B; Wolk, 9/17). Second, a 53rd-week comp worth 1.5-2 points. Third, Sail dilution of about $1.28 per share in 2027 if milestones are hit and J&J exercises the option, plus $0.08 from Firefly (7/29 8-K). Wolk guided 'equivalent reported growth' in 2027. Any hedge on that, or on 2027 EPS growth given the Sail dilution, lands on the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline print turned explicitly on next-year commentary. After the Q3 2025 call, which included next-year framing, the stock moved -0.03%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock fell about 5.9% between 9/28 and 10/2 as commentary turned to the $4B 2027 cliff, so some of this is in the price. Not fully priced because the contingent $1.28 Sail dilution is not in most 2027 EPS models; if it were, 2027 consensus EPS would sit visibly below the 2026 guide-plus-growth path. Management may defer all of it to 12/8, in which case this is about 0.
findings.independence: The Wolk LOE quantification (DB transcript, https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/johnson--johnson-at-deutsche-bank-healthcare-summit-growth-outlook-lifts-93CH-4906149) is independent of the 7/29 8-K. The 8-K is shared with the EPS-headline and guidance findings, but this finding lands on 2027, a different period.

baseline_tension: The findings offset, consistent with a balanced skew (+1.85) and a run-up that is flat over 20 days; nothing here contradicts the option market. The main tension is magnitude: options imply 3.0% against a 0.9% median historical reaction.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; this name sells beats, median 0.9%, July beat-and-raise -2.7%): pharma revenue-beat finding cut from +0.4 to +0.3 and guidance-raise finding from +0.4 to +0.3; print_vs_bar kept at +0.8 while expected_move is 0.
Rules 2 and 6 (one-offs and a disputed bar): the IPR&D EPS-headline finding is a guided one_off on a bar ranging $2.48-2.81, so cut from -0.3 to -0.2.
Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): MedTech cardio finding cut from -0.5 to -0.4 because pharma (about 65% of sales) is tracking above consensus.
Precedent check: the ortho-sale finding was cut from +0.3 to +0.2 after the 2025-10-14 separation announcement with Q3 results moved the stock -0.03%.
Rule 3: the 2027 commentary finding's own text says management may defer to 12/8 and that the 9/28-10/2 drop priced part of it, so cut from -0.3 to -0.2.
p_up moved from 51 to 50 (balanced evidence, guided items). abs_move_pct left at 2.8 per the core (uncertainty does not shrink it).
